requirement:
The requirements index links to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
`requirements.test-coverage.index.navigation` has one obligation: the requirements index must link to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter. The cited `requirements.test-coverage.index` adds that this holds whether the index is explicitly placed or automatically generated. Three marked tests cover those cases, and each asserts the link text itself.

- **Explicit index.** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` uses an index chapter placed at `appendix/requirements-index.md`. It asserts that exactly one sub-chapter named "Documented coverage gaps" exists, with path `appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md` and parent names `["Requirements index"]`. It also asserts that the index content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`, so the link target matches the subchapter's location.
- **Default index.** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` covers an automatically generated index with no marker. It asserts the same subchapter, with path `requirements-index/coverage.md`. It asserts the same link, `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`, in the index content.
- **Nested or renamed index.** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` puts the index at `reports.md` under a parent chapter. It runs with and without section numbers. It asserts the link `[Documented coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)` in the parent's content. It also asserts the subchapter's path and parent names, so the link points at the real subchapter.

These tests cover both placement modes and varied index paths, so a wrong or missing link would fail them. The requirement states no other obligations, so I found no gaps.
